text.en: The cooking gas in your kitchen, the petrol in a scooter and the wax in a candle are all made mostly of carbon and hydrogen. Such compounds are called hydrocarbons, and adding one more kind of atom changes their behaviour completely.

Organic compounds are first classified by the pattern of the carbon chain: open chain or acyclic compounds, and closed chain or cyclic compounds.
Open chain compounds with only C-C single bonds are saturated, like ethane C2H6; those with double or triple bonds are unsaturated, like ethene and ethyne.
Cyclic compounds are carbocyclic, with a ring of carbon only, such as cyclobutane and benzene, or heterocyclic, with a ring that also has another element, such as pyridine and furan.
Hydrocarbons are compounds of carbon and hydrogen only, and all other organic compounds are considered to be derived from them by replacing hydrogen atoms.
Alkanes have only single bonds and the general formula CnH2n+2, for example methane CH4, ethane C2H6, propane C3H8, butane C4H10 and pentane C5H12.
Alkenes have one or more C=C bonds and the formula CnH2n, such as ethene C2H4, propene C3H6, butene C4H8 and pentene C5H10.
Alkynes have a C triple bond C and the formula CnH2n-2, such as ethyne or acetylene C2H2, propyne C3H4, butyne C4H6 and pentyne C5H8.
Hydrocarbons are colourless and odourless, insoluble in water, their boiling point rises with the number of carbon atoms, and they burn in oxygen to give carbon dioxide and water; the lower ones are gases.
Alkanes are the least reactive and alkynes the most reactive because of the triple bond.
Test for unsaturation: add a few drops of bromine water; an alkene or alkyne decolourises it, but a saturated alkane does not.
A functional group is an atom or group of atoms that gives a compound its characteristic chemical properties; if one hydrogen of ethane is replaced by -OH, we get the alcohol ethanol, written R-OH.
Common classes are alcohol R-OH, aldehyde R-CHO, ketone R-CO-R, carboxylic acid R-COOH, ester R-COOR and ether R-O-R.
The chemical properties of a compound depend on its functional group, while its physical properties depend on the rest of the structure.

problem.en: Write the formula of the alkane, alkene and alkyne with 3 carbon atoms, and say how you would tell which is saturated.

text.en: Alkane: CnH2n+2 with n = 3 gives C3H8, propane.
Alkene: CnH2n with n = 3 gives C3H6, propene.

why.en: One double bond means two hydrogens fewer than the alkane.

text.en: Alkyne: CnH2n-2 with n = 3 gives C3H4, propyne.

why.en: A triple bond means four hydrogens fewer.

text.en: Add bromine water to each: propane leaves it brown, so it is saturated; propene and propyne decolourise it.

prompt.en: Describe alkanes, alkenes and alkynes with their formulae and explain what a functional group is.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking alkanes are the most reactive
Mixing up the general formulae of alkenes and alkynes

points.en: Alkanes CnH2n+2 are saturated; alkenes CnH2n and alkynes CnH2n-2 are unsaturated.
Unsaturated compounds decolourise bromine water; saturated ones do not.
A functional group (-OH, -CHO, -COOH and so on) decides the chemical properties.
Hydrocarbons burn in oxygen to give CO2 and water and are insoluble in water.
